policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV main text 'He will requite the evil unto mine enemies' renders the transitive hiphil qere yashiv (God requites); the textual_variant note 'Another reading is, The evil shall return' is the intransitive qal ketiv yashuv, which the ASV explicitly relegates to the margin. The wording distinguishes the qere.
